Changelog

Source: NEWS.md

tidylayouts 0.0.0.9000

  • New layout engine built on ggplot2 and grid; no longer depends on ggalign. Plots are aligned by their panel edges, also across nested rows and columns.
  • Removed row(), column() and grid(); use new_row(), new_column() and new_grid(). Their horizontal_align and vertical_align (defaults "left" and "bottom") place the plots of that row, column or grid; nested rows, columns and grids fill their space and use their own alignment. A grid shares row and column tracks.
  • New new_layout() builds a layout from a design string, e.g. "ABEF\nCDEF\nGGGG". Letters place the plots; by default each design line becomes a row (arrange_by = "row"), alternatively a column or a grid. Tags are numbered in reading order, and tag_group() works on its inputs. Plots keep their sizes; auto_width, auto_height, auto_margins_x and auto_margins_y change that for listed plots.
  • New new_row(), new_column() and new_grid() build a layout step by step: each call adds a row below, a column to the right, or a grid below everything built so far. They replace add_right() and add_below(). new_row(..., wrap = <mm>) breaks a long row into lines, like text in a word processor; new_column(..., wrap = <mm>) breaks a tall column into several columns; new_grid(..., wrap = <mm>) picks as many grid columns as fit.
  • New auto_width() and auto_height() let the layout decide a plot’s panel size; auto_margins() keeps the panel size and centers the plot in the spare space next to it. set_size() sets a fixed panel size in mm for tidyplots and plain ggplots.
  • New tag_group() lets several plots share one panel tag.
  • New save_layout() saves a figure at its exact physical size.
  • layout_tags() aligns tags at the top of each row and at the left edge of each column; layout_size() sets the figure size in mm.
  • spacer() without a size now absorbs leftover space.
  • Plot backgrounds are drawn before all plots, so axis labels sticking out past a plot are no longer covered by the neighbouring plot’s background.
  • layout_spacing(inner, outer) now sets the gaps between plots in mm (one value, or c(horizontal, vertical)), replacing the plots’ own margins, plus an optional outer margin around the figure.
  • Removed layout_alignment(); use horizontal_align and vertical_align.

Developed by Jan Broder Engler.
